title: Expressions and operators: grouping, values, and clear steps
lead: Break a formula into operands, predict the result, and rewrite a dense line as verifiable intermediate calculations.
why: Similar-looking formulas can describe different calculations. Precedence determines grouping rather than a universal execution order. The distinction prevents later mistakes involving state changes.
objectives: Identify operands, operator, type, and value in a simple expression.
Use parentheses and basic multiplicative versus additive precedence.
Distinguish grouping from operand evaluation order.
Extract intermediate quantities while preserving result and units.
prerequisites: Initialized ints, copying, assignment, and nested blocks.
Arithmetic of small integers. Multiple state changes in one complex expression are unnecessary here.

concepts.definition: A combination of operands and operations producing a typed value in our calculations.
A value or nested expression to which an operation applies.
A rule for grouping operators when parentheses are absent.
Grouping for operators at the same precedence level, not a general evaluation-order promise.
A named calculation result that can be observed and checked separately.

sections.title: Start with value and type
paragraphs: In count * unitPriceCents the names are operands and * multiplies them. When both are int and the result is representable, the expression also has type int. An expression need not mutate its operands: reading two values and producing a result differs from assignment.

int total = count * unitPriceCents; initializes total from the expression. std::cout << total; observes the value. This separates domain calculation, storage, and formatting. Annotate units: items × cents per item = cents.

sections.title: Precedence determines a grouping tree
paragraphs: 2 + 3 * 4 groups multiplication inside addition: it corresponds to 2 + (3 * 4), giving 14. (2 + 3) * 4 explicitly selects another calculation and gives 20. Parentheses do not request speed; they specify expression structure.

At this level + and − group left: 20 - 5 - 3 means (20 - 5) - 3, not 20 - (5 - 3). You need not memorize the entire operator table now. Apply the levels in use and add parentheses that clarify intention. Parentheses cannot rescue a domain formula that was chosen incorrectly.

sections.title: Grouping is not chronological order
paragraphs: The tree 2 + (3 * 4) describes value dependencies. It does not establish that the left operand always executes first in arbitrary C++. Our calculations have no changing operands, so stdout does not expose this distinction yet.

Increment and complex calls come later. Keep one understandable effect in its own statement. We do not run i++ + ++i as a puzzle: this style obscures sequencing rules and can have undefined behavior. Experimenting does not make a dangerous expression valid.

sections.title: Intermediate names expose the formula
paragraphs: unitPriceCents * count + shippingCents can be split into goodsCents and totalCents. Goods and shipping can then be checked separately. This does not create a dynamically linked formula: each statement computes its value when executed, as in the variables lesson.

Keep types and statement dependencies and do not introduce hidden rounding. The demonstrated split preserves the bounded integer calculation. Arbitrary rearrangements of floating-point operations can change rounding; this is not permission for every algebraic rewrite.

sections.title: A block groups a stage, not arithmetic
paragraphs: A nested block can limit temporary names. If a result is needed outside, declare and initialize the outer result first, then assign the calculation to it inside. Declaring another result inside hides the outer object rather than updating it.

Expression parentheses (a + b) and block braces { ... } have different roles. State what is grouped: formula operands or statements and scope. This is more useful than mechanically adding brackets everywhere.

sections.title: Checking readability through behavior preservation
paragraphs: Before editing, record the contract and several data sets. After extracting intermediate quantities compare the whole stdout and explain each stage in domain terms. Agreement only at zero price is a weak test that may fail to distinguish formulas.

The diagram shows one selected grouping. It is not a parser and does not establish arbitrary program evaluation order. The laboratory needs source, checks, and an equivalence explanation rather than merely an attractive tree screenshot.

experiments.title: Equivalent explicit parentheses
experiments.action: Replace 2 + 3 * 4 with 2 + (3 * 4) in the first example.
experiments.verification: Compare with the original and explain the unchanged grouping.

experiments.title: A weak test can hide a defect
experiments.action: Compare (price + shipping) * count and price * count + shipping with count=1, then count=3; use price=120 and shipping=40.
experiments.prediction: At 1 both give 160; at 3 they give 480 and 400.
experiments.verification: Choose the test that distinguishes the incorrect shipping formula.

diagnostics.cause: Parentheses grouped unit price with one-time shipping.
diagnostics.fix: Calculate goods first and add shipping once.

diagnostics.cause: Precedence was confused with general evaluation order.
diagnostics.fix: Describe the dependency tree and put effects in separate statements.

diagnostics.cause: A new inner result was declared.
diagnostics.fix: Assign the existing outer object instead of hiding it.

diagnosticExamples.title: Intentional: missing right operand
diagnosticExamples.explanation: + has no right operand. Restore the expression rather than guessing another type.

Three cases are recorded with expectations.
Precedence is distinguished from evaluation order.

assessment.question: What do parentheses specify in (a + b) * c?
Does a grouping tree establish every C++ operand evaluation order?
assessment.explanation: The tree describes value dependencies; sequencing is a separate concern.

reflection: Which test would detect shipping multiplied by count?
When is an intermediate name more useful than additional parentheses?
